description: Design for manufacturing: the process ladder (cheapest accessible method first), a layered DFM profile of machine and material limits with a status and a source on every value, process playbooks starting with 3D printing, the DfX checklist, design aids, and an independent DFM review before anything is made.

skills.summary: Start here for any mechanical design (a part, enclosure, bracket, mount, jig, case or fixture; a board moved into CAD to build around it): establish the manufacturing process (asked or inferred; FDM by default, cheapest rung first), resolve the DFM profile, load the process playbook, balance style against the process limits, record waivers, prove risky fits with a coupon or a printed slice, and cross-check with DfX

Design rules for 3D printed parts, FDM first: walls, overhangs, bridges, holes, orientation, materials, fits and clearances per side, heat-set inserts, captured nuts, embedded magnets, other printing processes, and test coupons

Independent check of a model against the resolved DFM profile and the process playbook before it is made: each value measured or read first, then compared; findings carry rule, value, limit, status, source and location, with OK / FAILED / NOT CHECKED / WAIVED results that advise and never block
